metadata.title: Binary companions of nearby supernova remnants found with Gaia

evidence.quote: runaway TYC 2688-1556-1 associated with the Cygnus Loop is a hypervelocity star.

There is a small probability that the 2 M candidate
runaway TYC 2688-1556-1 associated with the Cygnus Loop is a hypervelocity star.

If the star is from this mode, it is likely unbound
from the Milky Way.

values.condition: Median posterior predicted heliocentric radial velocity of TYC 2688-1556-1 under the runaway-companion model; uncertainty is the reported posterior uncertainty.

notes: TYC 2688-1556-1: the paper states only a conditional Galactic-unbound possibility—the abstract calls it a possible hypervelocity star (T:p1-b7), and Section 5.2 says it is likely unbound only if it originated in the second posterior mode (T:p10-b3); the conclusion still describes a possible hypervelocity star (T:p15-b1), and it remains among the paper’s four candidates (T:p14-b5). No Gaia source ID is supplied; the TYC designation is the only supported star identifier.

TYC 2688-1556-1: T:p9-b1 (Table 4) lists dSNR = 0.57 ± 0.07 kpc for TYC 2688-1556-1, but dSNR is explicitly the distance to the SNR centre, not the star's heliocentric distance, so it is not recorded as the star's distance. In T:p10-b3 the declination proper motion is transcribed as “−21 03”; the decimal point is missing, and I record −21.03 based on the reported uncertainty and context. A second posterior mode predicts a heliocentric radial velocity of about +600 or −600 km/s if the star belongs to that high-velocity mode (T:p10-b3), but the paper does not give a unique sign or a single numerical value, so it is not separately entered. No numerical parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.
